solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Quote Italian in church

indicators.note: in tells us the Italian letters are placed within the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: Someone quotes an Italian speaker heard during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To quote a source is to cite it; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Film container actors originally employed around filming location

indicators.note: around says the actors-plus-initial letters go round the filming location

parts.note: the cast is the company of actors in a production
a set is where a film is shot

indicators.note: originally picks the opening letter of the word employed

explanation.surface: Actors originally hired were placed around the shoot with a reel of film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' suggests cinema, but the container is the cartridge loaded into a camera; 'around' wraps the actors-plus-initial group about the location.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette is a sealed case holding film or tape for loading into a camera or player.

clue.text: It isn't commonly a stain or blemish

definitions.meaning: '... is the colloquial contraction of it ain't, a nonstandard form of it isn't
a mark of corruption or discredit

explanation.surface: A colloquial denial that something is a stain or blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a trace of contamination or moral blemish, as in the taint of scandal.

clue.text: In class a boy is relaxed and friendly

parts.note: a form is a class in a British school
Al is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A schoolboy in the class is described as easy-going and sociable.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal manner is casual, relaxed and friendly rather than stiff.

clue.text: Start here, only travelling towards John o'Groats, say?

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters moving about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Travel advice: start here and head only to the far tip of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: John o'Groats is a village at the north-east tip of mainland Scotland; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading to that Scottish settlement from most of Britain means going up and to the right on the map.

clue.text: Tender Conservative not opening box

indicators.note: not opening says the first letter, the Conservative abbreviation, is missing from the start of the box

parts.note: a coffer is a strongbox

explanation.surface: A tender Conservative politician refuses to open a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like an adjective (soft) but is the verb or noun for proposing.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender something is to offer it formally, as in tendering a bid.

clue.text: Friend carrying revolutionary bladed weapon

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the friend letters hold the revolutionary

parts.note: a mate is a friend
Che Guevara, the Argentine-born guerrilla

explanation.surface: A friend is carrying a revolutionary's bladed weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy knife used as a tool and a weapon.

clue.text: Device a shoemaker uses after everything else?

definitions.meaning: a cobbler's foot-shaped block for shaping shoes
coming at the very end, final

explanation.surface: A shoemaker's tool, perhaps used once everything else is done.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the cobbler's foot-shaped form and final in order.

clue.text: Posh bird, some say, in East African state

parts.note: U means upper-class or posh

indicators.note: some say signals that the bird is spoken, giving a word of similar sound

parts.note: a gander is a male goose

explanation.surface: A grand bird, according to some, is found in an East African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Uganda is a landlocked republic in East Africa.

clue.text: Lively person's son, a footballer, perhaps

parts.note: a winger is a footballer who plays out wide, given here as an example

explanation.surface: A proud parent describes their son, a footballer, as a lively character.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'person' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A swinger is a fashionable, lively, sociable type, especially in 1960s slang.

clue.text: Endless to-do about commander's centre of activity

indicators.note: about means going round, so the trimmed fuss is wrapped around the commander
endless says the last letter of the word for a to-do is cut off

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss, a commotion
OC is Officer Commanding; the 's links to the definition

explanation.surface: A commander's office is the scene of constant fuss and bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims FUSS to FUS, which goes 'about' OC to give F-OC-US.
explanation.definitionFit: The focus of something is its central point, where activity concentrates.

clue.text: Consumed in college, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for the college is to be said aloud

parts.note: Eton College is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Something was eaten at college, or so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the elite English school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been consumed has been eaten; both are past participles.

clue.text: Messenger god immersed in another message

indicators.note: immersed in says the letters lie submerged inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A messenger god is somehow buried in a further piece of correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this Olympian was the winged herald of the gods.

clue.text: Raucous start to squabble over ballistic missile

indicators.note: over places the first piece above the second in this down entry
start to picks the opening letter of the word squabble

parts.note: Trident is the submarine-launched ballistic missile

explanation.surface: A noisy beginning to an argument about nuclear missiles.
explanation.walkthrough: Trident is the UK's nuclear deterrent missile system.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice is loud and harsh, so raucous.

clue.text: But would a driver's unwelcome adviser withdraw thus?

definitions.text: But would a driver's unwelcome adviser withdraw thus?

parts.words: But would a driver's unwelcome adviser withdraw thus?
parts.note: a back-seat driver gives unwanted advice; the phrase for stepping back from involvement literally describes them retreating to a rear seat

explanation.surface: Wishing an interfering passenger would stop advising the driver.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to withdraw from an active role, here played literally as a passenger moving rearward.

clue.text: Clever Dick takes risk ultimately climbing on barrier

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of the word risk
climbing in a down entry means the word on is read upwards

parts.note: a wall is a barrier

explanation.surface: A smart alec takes a final risk scaling a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clever Dick' is British slang for a show-off; 'takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever dick is a smug person who acts as if they have all the answers.

clue.text: Girl describing a run or a martial art

indicators.note: describing in the sense of drawing a line around, so the girl encloses the letters

parts.note: Kate is a girl's name
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A girl describing a jog or a fighting discipline she does.
explanation.definitionFit: Karate is a Japanese unarmed combat system using strikes and kicks.

clue.text: Possibly fellow Lithuanian's element?

parts.note: co- is the prefix for a fellow or joint partner, as in co-worker
a Lithuanian is a Balt, a native of a Baltic state

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a compatriot from Lithuania has some particular quality or element.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt is a metallic chemical element, atomic number 27.

clue.text: Book of maps finally almost finished

indicators.note: almost means the phrase is nearly complete, its last letter dropped

parts.note: finally means at last

explanation.surface: A book of maps is finally almost done.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound collection of maps.

clue.text: Spiritual leader's tailless pet?

indicators.note: tailless says the final letter of the word for the pet is lopped off

parts.note: a rabbit is a common pet

explanation.surface: A religious leader owns a pet with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'leader' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher and leader of a congregation.

clue.text: Large circle adopting northern game

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the large-and-circle letters take in the northern letter

parts.note: big means large
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: A large circle of players takes up a northern game.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is a numbers game of chance played with cards.

clue.text: Basil, perhaps — a girl's boyfriend at first

parts.note: her means belonging to a girl

indicators.note: at first selects the initial letter of the word boyfriend

explanation.surface: A man called Basil was, at first, a girl's boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basil' looks like a man's name but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is an example of a culinary plant used for flavouring.

clue.text: Send message to European man verbally

indicators.note: verbally signals that the word for man is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a man is a male

explanation.surface: Sending a message to a European man by word of mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: To email someone is to send them an electronic message.

clue.text: Attendants English can put in French street

indicators.note: put in says the English and can letters are placed inside the street

parts.note: rue is French for street
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Servants are carrying an English tin along a Parisian street.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is a group of attendants accompanying an important person.

clue.text: Top score? A sucker might get it!

definitions.meaning: hitting the centre of a dartboard gives a high score
a striped boiled mint sweet sucked slowly, so a sucker might be given one; also a gullible person might be the target

explanation.surface: A top score, and something a dupe might receive.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both the dartboard centre and a hard round peppermint sweet popular in Britain.

clue.text: Club accommodating old vessel

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so the club letters hold the old letter

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sport

explanation.surface: A club with room for an old ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat is a vessel for travelling on water.
